grammar.title: Like doing or want to do
grammar.explanation:
Some verbs love -ing. After **like** and **enjoy**, we use verb + -ing. No **to** in the middle.

Some verbs love **to**. After **want** and **need**, we use **to** + verb.

A common mistake: do not say **like to reading**. Say **like reading**.
examples: Sara *likes reading* books at the library. (like + -ing)
The children *enjoy learning* at the school. (enjoy + -ing)
I *want to sleep* in a hotel in the city. (want + to)
We *need to go* back to the village. (need + to)

practice.q: Complete: I like ___ in the city. (walk / to walk)
practice.a: walk — like + -ing: I like walking in the city.

practice.q: Complete: She wants ___ at a hotel. (sleep / to sleep)
practice.a: to sleep — want + to: She wants to sleep at a hotel.
